<objective>
Author the two code artifacts of SC5's diner design vocabulary: the full Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011
Annex II allergen set in Hungarian, English and Romanian, and the diner-facing copy deck carrying the
D-07 last-good banner, the language-detection disclosure, the always-present allergen disclaimer, and
the diner empty states.

Purpose: the imported `qr-menu` template ships **7 of the 14** EU allergens while its README claims
"Allergens are the EU set" — a false claim on the one display PROJECT.md names as legally load-bearing,
and it omits **peanuts** as a category distinct from tree nuts. Cena's obligation is not to *declare*
allergens — the restaurant does that — it is to **not make compliance structurally impossible**. A
7-value vocabulary means a restaurant serving prawns, satay, hummus or mussels physically cannot declare
them. Research resolved this as vocabulary in 01.1, filtering in Phase 3; leaving it to Phase 3 repeats
exactly the pattern D-06 was written to prevent — a legal gate invented under time pressure.

Output: `lib/allergens.ts`, `lib/diner-copy.ts`, and their two tests.

**Enabling relationship:** this plan delivers no requirement ID. It is the artifact half of SC5, consumed
by DINE-06 (Phase 3), DINE-04 and MENU-10 (Phase 2), LANG-05/06 (Phase 5) and INGEST-04/06 (Phase 7).

**It also carries one decided constraint that has no other home in this phase.** RESEARCH Open Question 9 —
does the QR payload encode the language — is answered in `01.1-UI-SPEC.md` § Language (LANG-05, LANG-06):
**yes**, as `/menu/[slug]/[defaultLang]`, against a `/menu/[slug]/[lang]` static page set. 01.1 builds no
route, so nothing here implements it; but `lib/diner-copy.ts` owns the `languageDetected` string that only
exists because negotiation is a 307, which makes this module the honest place to write the shape down.
Task 2 records it in the module header. Deciding it late is not a refactor — DINE-01 prints the payload onto
a laminated table card, so a later change is a physical re-print of every table in every venue.

**SC5 is the phase's weakest-measured criterion and this plan says so rather than papering over it.**
Three of its four sub-claims are assertable — residue enumeration (plan 01.1-14), the 14-allergen
vocabulary (here), and the Copywriting Contract rows (here and plan 01.1-03). The fourth — "mobile-first,
intentional and attractive" — is not a property a unit test can assert and is a human gate at
`/gsd-ui-review`.

**Translation caveat, carried forward not resolved.** The HU/EN/RO strings lifted from the template read
as idiomatic and were authored alongside HU-first menu content, but **no native speaker has reviewed
them**, and the three D-07 strings were newly authored in `01.1-UI-SPEC.md` under the same caveat. Treat
as a strong starting point requiring review, not as final copy. Record this in the module headers.
</objective>

    Write the failing test first, then the implementation.

    Create `lib/allergens.ts` following `lib/copy.ts`'s shape: a header comment block, one nested `const`

    The 14 keys are Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 Annex II's **categories**, not a finer ingredient list —
    categories are what the regulation mandates and what a restaurant can realistically maintain:
    `gluten`, `crustaceans`, `eggs`, `fish`, `peanuts`, `soybeans`, `milk`, `nuts`, `celery`, `mustard`,
    `sesame`, `sulphites`, `lupin`, `molluscs`.

    preferences; the fourth is a decided constraint this module is the only place in the phase to carry:

    1. **The D-07 banner replaces the template's string entirely.** The template tells the diner their
       network dropped and that prices will refresh once it returns. The architecture is ISR stale-serve —
       the page was prerendered and served from the edge, and what failed is *background regeneration*.
       **The diner's own connection may be perfectly healthy.** A string blaming their network is misleading
       and implies an auto-refresh the page does not perform. The banner is timestamped and specific because
       a bare "Saved menu" cannot distinguish
       five minutes from five weeks, and PROJECT.md names the risk directly: a diner ordering something that
       has been off for a month and credibility is gone.
    2. **The allergen disclaimer is always present and never dismissible.** The declaration obligation sits
       with the restaurant; this is the posture the EU food-information constraint requires.
    3. **The `{HH:mm}` timestamp must be real at render time.** The template's `updatedLine` is the
       hardcoded literal `4 · 8 · 19:04` — a footer that *looks* like it shows freshness and does not. Phase 2
       carries a genuine `generatedAt` from the prerender. The honest staleness signal is prerender age,

<threat_model>
**Review level: OWASP ASVS L1.** This is the level appropriate to a phase that changes no auth logic, no authorization boundary and no data path — 01.1 is a visual and vocabulary migration, and every plan that touches a security-relevant file holds it byte-identical under a `git diff` gate rather than reviewing it. **Block on: `high`.** Every threat rated `high` or `critical` carries a `mitigate` disposition with a named, gated implementation; `medium` and `low` may carry `accept` with a stated rationale.

## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| restaurant-declared allergen data → diner | The diner reads allergen chips and makes a health decision. The vocabulary constrains what a restaurant is able to declare at all. |
| prerender age → diner | The last-good banner is the only signal that the menu the diner is reading may be stale. |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-01.1-11 | Information Disclosure | `lib/allergens.ts` vocabulary completeness | high | mitigate | The 14-key Annex II set with `peanuts` distinct from `nuts`, asserted by `tests/lib/allergens.test.ts` with the regulation cited in the failure message. A 7-value vocabulary makes declaration structurally impossible for prawns, satay, hummus and mussels. |
| T-01.1-19 | Repudiation | Missing or dismissible allergen disclaimer | high | mitigate | The disclaimer is a contracted always-present, never-dismissible string in all three languages, and absence of a chip is contractually never rendered as "free of" — the declaration obligation stays with the restaurant. |
| T-01.1-20 | Spoofing | Last-good banner implying freshness it does not have | high | mitigate | The D-07 string is timestamped with a real `{HH:mm}`, warns about sold-out dishes, and makes no reconnect promise. A negative grep for reconnect language is an acceptance criterion, so the template's wrong failure model cannot be carried in. |
| T-01.1-21 | Tampering | Un-reviewed HU/RO translations shipping as final | medium | accept | Recorded in both module headers as a strong starting point requiring native-speaker review, and carried forward as a named open item rather than silently assumed correct. |
</threat_model>

## Explicitly dismissed UI considerations (accounted, not dropped)

`01.1-UI-SPEC.md` § UI Considerations marks five considerations in this plan's scope as dismissed with a
stated reason. They are recorded here so the count reconciles and none is a silent drop:

| Element | Consideration | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| E2 category rail | error | Derived at prerender from the same section data as the list; no independent fetch, therefore no independent failure mode |
| E3 item detail sheet | error | No fetch on open, so there is no failure path to design for |
| E4 last-good banner | loading | Server-rendered with the page from prerender age; there is no in-flight state to show |
| E6 allergen / dietary chips | error | Chips render from prerendered item data with no independent fetch; the legal fallback for missing data is the always-present disclaimer, already contracted |
| E7 dietary filter chips | error | A pure in-memory predicate over prerendered data has no failure path |
